title: Education and HIV

blocks.heading: Education and HIV
blocks.text: Accurate education can counter HIV misinformation, reduce stigma and help people understand prevention and qualified support routes. It should protect privacy and continued participation. Sharing classrooms, food or ordinary contact does not transmit HIV; no learner should be asked to disclose status in a class exercise.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: An invented school introduces accurate HIV education and a confidential route for reporting discrimination. Explaining that ordinary classroom contact does not transmit HIV can address a false belief, while staff action is needed when exclusion continues. Information and supportive behaviour reinforce each other; learners should not be required to identify anyone’s health status.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
blocks.repair_note: Codex targeted third-review repairs R3-01–R3-10; pre-repair snapshot retained in review/repairs/round3/.

blocks.heading: Health information source
blocks.text: The [WHO HIV fact sheet](https://www.who.int/en/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hiv-aids), checked 20 October 2026, supports the ordinary-contact distinction used here. Educational inclusion is not an individual clinical assessment, and classmates should not be asked to investigate or disclose health status.
